patch: Update PHP 8.3 from 8.3.30 to 8.3.36 or newer.
Update the PHP runtime itself. Updating WordPress, Laravel or any app does not update PHP; it comes from the server package, the host panel, or the container image.
Restart Apache, PHP-FPM and any long-running PHP workers after updating.
disable: Set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 in php.ini or the PHP-FPM pool config, then restart every worker. Do NOT rely on ini_set() or .user.ini. This removes a required condition for CVE-2026-115560 and blocks one PHP2Shell path. Trade-off: upload progress bars stop working.

Until you can update (reduces exposure, does NOT fix): set memory_limit=-1 so apps cannot override it, keep post_max_size low, and enforce request-size limits at the web server or proxy. Do not use RLIMIT_AS or RLIMIT_DATA.
Search the app code for session.serialize_handler. The risky pattern is switching it with ini_set() before session_start(). local-audit.js does this for you.
notes: This looks like a distro build. Vendors backport fixes without changing version numbers, so check the package changelog before trusting the version string.
covered: PHP version the site discloses in response headers, compared with the fixed releases (8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, 8.2.35)

Server hints that raise risk (mod_php) and Cloudflare in front
Status of CVE-2026-115560 (no fixed release exists yet)
notCovered: Whether the exploit actually works. This is a passive check; it sends no attack traffic

Distro backports: a fixed package can show an old version number
Whether workers were restarted after patching
session.upload_progress.enabled, memory limits and other settings: not visible from outside
App code that switches session.serialize_handler (needed for CVE-2026-115560). Use local-audit.js on the server

On Debian, Ubuntu or RHEL builds, check the package changelog for CVE-2026-109618; vendors backport fixes under old version numbers.
If patched, still confirm Apache and PHP-FPM were restarted afterward.
disable: Set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 in php.ini or the PHP-FPM pool config, then restart every worker. Do NOT rely on ini_set() or .user.ini. This removes a required condition for CVE-2026-115560 and blocks one PHP2Shell path. Trade-off: upload progress bars stop working.
Search the app code for session.serialize_handler. The risky pattern is switching it with ini_set() before session_start(). local-audit.js does this for you.
covered: PHP version the site discloses in response headers, compared with the fixed releases (8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, 8.2.35)
Signs the site runs PHP (PHPSESSID cookie, WordPress markers, PHP banners)
Server hints that raise risk (mod_php) and Cloudflare in front
Status of CVE-2026-115560 (no fixed release exists yet)
notCovered: Whether the exploit actually works. This is a passive check; it sends no attack traffic
Sites that hide their version (expose_php=Off or a proxy strips headers). They come back "unknown"
Distro backports: a fixed package can show an old version number
Whether workers were restarted after patching
session.upload_progress.enabled, memory limits and other settings: not visible from outside
App code that switches session.serialize_handler (needed for CVE-2026-115560). Use local-audit.js on the server
Other PHP, CMS or plugin vulnerabilities
Multiple PHP versions behind one domain, or a different PHP on the CLI than on the web

hidden-wordpress.caveat: Passive check: reads response headers only. It does not test the exploit.

headline.title: No PHP detected
headline.sub: Nothing here points to PHP. This is not proof the site is safe.

cves.title: RCE via out-of-memory corruption (CVSS v4 9.2)
cves.detail: Only updating PHP fixes this. No setting fully mitigates it.

cves.title: RCE via stale global state (CVSS v4 9.2)
cves.detail: Updating is the only complete fix. Turning off session upload progress blocks the confirmed session paths but not other variants.

cves.title: Possible code execution in an uncommon session setup
cves.detail: No fixed PHP release exists yet, so no version can be called patched. Exposure depends on server config and app code, which cannot be seen from outside.
